Compute the quadratic form $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ , for $$A = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ and
Find the matrix of the quadratic form. Assume $$\textbf{x}$$ is in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ .
Find the matrix of the quadratic form. Assume $$\textbf{x}$$ is in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ .

Make a change of variable, $$\textbf{x} = P\textbf{y}$$ , that transforms the quadratic form $$x_{1}^{2} + 10x_{1}x_{2} + x_{2}^{2}$$ into a quadratic form with no cross-product term. Give $$P$$ and the new quadratic form.
Let $$A$$ be the matrix of the quadratic form $$9 x_{1}^{2} + 7 x_{2}^{2} + 11 x_{3}^{2} - 8 x_{1} x_{2} + 8 x_{1} x_{3}$$

It can be shown that the eigenvalues of $$A$$ are $$3$$ , $$9$$ , and $$15$$ . Give $$P$$ and the new quadratic form.

exercise_group.instruction: Classify the quadratic forms in Exercises 9–18. Then make a change of variable, $$\textbf{x} = P\textbf{y}$$ , that transforms the quadratic form into one with no cross-product term. Write the new quadratic form. Construct $$P$$ using the methods of Section 7.1.

problem.paragraph: What is the largest possible value of the quadratic form $$5x_{1}^{2} + 8x_{2}^{2}$$ if $$\textbf{x} = (x_{1},x_{2})$$ and $$\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x} = 1,$$ that is, if $$x_{1}^{2} + x_{2}^{2} = 1$$ ? (Try some examples of $$\textbf{x}$$ .)
What is the largest value of the quadratic form $$5x_{1}^{2} - 3x_{2}^{2}$$ if $$\textbf{x}^{T}\textbf{x} = 1$$ ?

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 21–30, matrices are $$n \times n$$ and vectors are in $$\textbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ . Mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) The matrix of a quadratic form is a symmetric matrix.
(T/F) The expression $$\text{∥} \textbf{x} \text{∥} ^{2}$$ is not a quadratic form.
(T/F) A quadratic form has no cross-product terms if and only if the matrix of the quadratic form is a diagonal matrix.

(T/F) If $$A$$ is symmetric and $$P$$ is an orthogonal matrix, then the change of variable $$\textbf{x} = P\textbf{y}$$ transforms $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ into a quadratic form with no cross-product term.
(T/F) The principal axes of a quadratic form $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ are eigenvectors of $$A$$ .
(T/F) If the eigenvalues of a symmetric matrix $$A$$ are all positive, then the quadratic form $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ is positive definite.
(T/F) A positive definite quadratic form $$Q$$ satisfies $$Q(\textbf{x}) > 0$$ for all $$\textbf{x}$$ in $$\textbf{\mathbb{R}}^{n}$$ .
(T/F) An indefinite quadratic form is neither positive semidefinite nor negative semidefinite.
(T/F) A Cholesky factorization of a symmetric matrix $$A$$ has the form $$A = R^{T} R$$ , for an upper triangular matrix $$R$$ with positive diagonal entries.
(T/F) If $$A$$ is symmetric and the quadratic form $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ has only negative values for $$\textbf{x} \neq \textbf{0}$$ , then the eigenvalues of $$A$$ are all positive.

exercise_group.instruction: Exercises 31 and 32 show how to classify a quadratic form $$Q(\textbf{x}) = \textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ , when $$A = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} a & b \\ b & d \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ and $$\det A \neq 0$$ , without finding the eigenvalues of $$A$$ .

problem.paragraph: If $$\text{λ} _{1}$$ and $$\text{λ} _{2}$$ are the eigenvalues of $$A$$ , then the characteristic polynomial of $$A$$ can be written in two ways: $$\det(A - \text{λ} I)$$ and $$( \text{λ} - \text{λ} _{1})( \text{λ} - \text{λ} _{2})$$ . Use this fact to show that $$\text{λ} _{1} + \text{λ} _{2} = a + d$$ (the diagonal entries of $$A$$ ) and $$\text{λ} _{1} \text{λ} _{2} = \det A$$ .
Verify the following statements:

list.item: $$Q$$ is positive definite if $$\det A > 0$$ and $$a > 0$$ .
$$Q$$ is negative definite if $$\det A > 0$$ and $$a < 0$$ .

problem.paragraph: Show that if $$B$$ is $$m \times n$$ , then $$B^{T}B$$ is positive semidefinite; and if $$B$$ is $$n \times n$$ and invertible, then $$B^{T}B$$ is positive definite.

Show that if an $$n \times n$$ matrix $$A$$ is positive definite, then there exists a positive definite matrix $$B$$ such that $$A = B^{T}B$$ . [Hint: Write $$A = {PDP}^{T}$$ , with $$P^{T} = P^{- 1}$$ . Produce a diagonal matrix $$C$$ such that $$D = C^{T}C$$ , and let $$B = PCP^{T}$$ . Show that $$B$$ works.]
Let $$A$$ and $$B$$ be symmetric $$n \times n$$ matrices whose eigenvalues are all positive. Show that the eigenvalues of $$A + B$$ are all positive. [Hint: Consider quadratic forms.]

Let $$A$$ be an $$n \times n$$ invertible symmetric matrix. Show that if the quadratic form $$\textbf{x}^{T}A\textbf{x}$$ is positive definite, then so is the quadratic form $$\textbf{x}^{T}A^{- 1}\textbf{x}$$ . [Hint: Consider eigenvalues.]
